title: 03. Functions: **kwargs — Variable Keyword Arguments
summary: kwargs lets a function accept any number of keyword arguments. The collects all extra keyword arguments into a dictionary.

sections.title: Explanation (Like You're a Junior Developer)
sections.body:
`**kwargs` lets a function accept **any number of keyword arguments**. The `**` collects all extra keyword arguments into a **dictionary**.

**Real-world analogy:** Think of `**kwargs` like a hotel check-in form with "special requests" section. The hotel knows the standard fields (name, room type, dates) but also has an open section for anything extra: "early check-in", "birthday cake", "extra pillows", "sea view". They don't know in advance what you'll put there — but they collect whatever extra preferences you specify.

```
def hotel_booking(name, room_type, **special_requests):
                                    ↑
                    collects all extra keyword args as dict

hotel_booking("Alice", "deluxe",
              early_checkin=True,
              birthday_cake=True,
              sea_view=True)
# special_requests = {
#     'early_checkin': True,
#     'birthday_cake': True,
#     'sea_view': True
# }
```

**Important facts about `**kwargs`:**
- `kwargs` is just convention — can name it anything: `**options`, `**config`, `**data`
- It's ALWAYS a **dict** inside the function
- Must come LAST in the parameter list
- Cannot have duplicate keyword arguments

sections.title: 5 Examples
sections.body: **What this code covers** - Accept any user fields as keyword arguments - Accepts absolutely anything - Wrapper around print() — same interface - Flexible database configuration using **kwargs - Process the dict normally - Pass any keyword arguments! - Positional args: (1, 2, 3) - Keyword args: {'name': 'Alice', 'age': 28, 'active': True} **Defines:** `create_user()`, `ultimate_function()`, `my_print()`, `DatabaseConfig`, `make_request()`, `html_element()` **Example 1 — Basic **kwargs** ```python def create_user(**user_data): """Accept any user fields as keyword arguments""" print(f"Type: {type(user_data)}") # print(f"Data: {user_data}") # Process the dict normally if "name" not in user_data: raise ValueError("'name' is required") return {"id": 1, **user_data} # Unpack into result dict # Pass any keyword arguments! user1 = create_user(name="Alice", age=28, city="NYC") user2 = create_user(name="Bob", email="bob@email.com", role="admin", active=True) user3 = create_user(name="Charlie") # Minimal print(user1) # {'id': 1, 'name': 'Alice', 'age': 28, 'city': 'NYC'} print(user2) # {'id': 1, 'name': 'Bob', 'email': 'bob@email.com', ...} ``` **Example 2 — Combining *args and **kwargs** ```python def ultimate_function(*args, **kwargs): """Accepts absolutely anything""" print(f"Positional args: {args}") print(f"Keyword args: {kwargs}") print(f"Total args: {len(args) + len(kwargs)}") ultimate_function(1, 2, 3, name="Alice", age=28, active=True) # Positional args: (1, 2, 3) # Keyword args: {'name': 'Alice', 'age': 28, 'active': True} # Total args: 6 # ─── Classic wrapper pattern ─── def my_print(*args, **kwargs): """Wrapper around print() — same interface""" print("[LOG]", *args, **kwargs) # Pass everything through! my_print("Hello", "World", sep="-", end="!\n") # [LOG] Hello-World! ``` **Example 3 — **kwargs for Configuration Objects** ```python class DatabaseConfig: """Flexible database configuration using **kwargs""" DEFAULTS = { "host": "localhost", "port": 5432, "database": "myapp", "username": "postgres", "password": "", "pool_size": 5, "timeout": 30, "ssl": False, "charset": "utf8" } def __init__(self, **kwargs): # Start with defaults, then override with provided values config = {**self.DEFAULTS, **kwargs} # kwargs override defaults # Validate unknown keys unknown = set(kwargs.keys()) - set(self.DEFAULTS.keys()) if unknown: raise ValueError(f"Unknown config options: {unknown}") # Set as attributes for key, value in config.items(): setattr(self, key, value) def connection_string(self): return (f"postgresql://{self.username}:{self.password}" f"@{self.host}:{self.port}/{self.database}") # Minimal config — uses all defaults dev_config = DatabaseConfig(database="dev_db") # Override specific settings prod_config = DatabaseConfig( host="prod.db.company.com", database="prod_app", username="app_user", password="s3cur3p@ss", pool_size=20, ssl=True, timeout=60 ) print(prod_config.connection_string()) ``` **Example 4 — **kwargs for Flexible API Clients** ```python import json def make_request(method, url, **kwargs): """ Flexible HTTP request builder. **kwargs passed directly to underlying library. """ # Extract known options we handle specially auth_token = kwargs.pop("auth_token", None) retry = kwargs.pop("retry", True) timeout = kwargs.pop("timeout", 30) # Build headers headers = kwargs.pop("headers", {}) if auth_token: headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {auth_token}" # Log the request (without sensitive data) safe_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in kwargs.items() if k != "data"} print(f"🌐 {method.upper()} {url}") print(f" Headers: {list(headers.keys())}") print(f" Options: {safe_kwargs}") print(f" Timeout: {timeout}s, Retry: {retry}") # In real code: return requests.request(method, url, # headers=headers, timeout=timeout, **kwargs) return {"status": 200, "url": url} # Flexible usage — pass any options make_request("GET", "/users", auth_token="abc123", params={"page": 1}) make_request( "POST", "/orders", auth_token="abc123", json={"product_id": 42, "quantity": 3}, timeout=60, retry=False, headers={"X-Request-ID": "req-001"} ) ``` **Example 5 — **kwargs for Dynamic HTML/Template Building** ```python def html_element(tag, *children, **attributes): """ Build HTML elements dynamically. tag: HTML tag name *children: child elements or text content **attributes: HTML attributes as keyword args """ # Special handling for Python reserved words # 'class' → 'class_', 'for' → 'for_' attrs = {} for key, value in attributes.items(): attr_name = key.rstrip("_") # Remove trailing underscore if isinstance(value, bool): if value: attrs[attr_name] = attr_name # e.g., disabled="disabled" else: attrs[attr_name] = str(value) attr_str = " ".join(f'{k}="{v}"' for k, v in attrs.items()) open_tag = f"<{tag} {attr_str}>" if attr_str else f"<{tag}>" content = "".join(str(c) for c in children) return f"{open_tag}{content}" # Build HTML! button = html_element("button", "Click Me!", class_="btn btn-primary", id="submit-btn", disabled=False, data_action="submit" ) print(button) # link = html_element("a", "Visit Website", href="https://example.com", target="_blank", class_="external-link" ) print(link) # Visit Website ```
